title: "Demo: live scopes"
engine: markdown
---

Drag the person. The value in the code changes, **exactly that code** runs in R in your browser, and the force arrow and the equation are filled in with the values from R. Changed values light up and fade. Add `?debug` to the page address to see timings.

:::: {.live #springs}
All examples in this section use the same spring:

```r
k  <- 2     # spring constant [N/m]
L0 <- 2     # rest length [m]
```

```{.r .hidden}
# Stiffness matrix of one spring (hidden on the page, but part of the full code)
spring_matrix <- function(k) k * matrix(c(1, -1, -1, 1), 2, 2)
```

The force on the person is $F = -k\,(x_1 - L_0)$.

::: {.live figure="spring1"}
```r
x1 <- 3
F  <- -k * (x1 - L0)
```

$$
F = -k\,(x_1 - L_0) = -{{k}}\,({{x1}} - {{L0}}) = {{F}}\ \mathrm{N}
$$
:::

## Matrices and vectors

A slot can hold a whole matrix or vector: `\mat{ {{K}} }` expands to the rows of `K`. Here the same spring is written with its stiffness matrix: the forces at the two ends are $f = K u$.

::: {.live figure="spring1"}
```r
x1 <- 2.5
K  <- spring_matrix(k)
u  <- c(0, x1 - L0)
f  <- K %*% u
F  <- -f[2]
```

$$
\mat{ {{f}} } = \mat{ {{K}} } \mat{ {{u|3}} }
$$
:::

## Changing the spring everywhere

Both examples above take `k` from the code at the top of the section. Now we can check what happens when we change the spring: every example in the section updates.

::: {.live-slider input="k" min="0.5" max="5" step="0.1" color="pen2"}
Spring constant
:::

## How this page is written

````markdown
:::: {.live #springs}
```r
k  <- 2     # spring constant [N/m]
L0 <- 2     # rest length [m]
```

```{.r .hidden}
spring_matrix <- function(k) k * matrix(c(1, -1, -1, 1), 2, 2)
```

::: {.live figure="spring1"}
```r
x1 <- 3
F  <- -k * (x1 - L0)
```

$$
F = -k\,(x_1 - L_0) = -{{k}}\,({{x1}} - {{L0}}) = {{F}}\ \mathrm{N}
$$
:::

…

::: {.live-slider input="k" min="0.5" max="5" step="0.1" color="pen2"}
Spring constant
:::
::::
````

- `:::: {.live}` is a **scope**. Its R code runs in its own environment, and scopes inside it see its variables (R's usual lookup through parent environments). An inner scope that assigns `k` itself gets its own `k`.
- The figure module `lib/js/figures/spring1.js` declares that the reader changes `x1`, and that it needs `L0` and `F` back from R. Dragging reruns only the figure's own scope.
- The slider changes `k`, which is assigned in the outer scope, so it reruns the outer scope and every scope inside it.
- Each `{{{expr}}}` in an equation is evaluated in R in its scope, and formatted by `tex_body()` from `lib/R/tex.R` (`{{{F|2}}}` would use 2 significant digits).
- **Full code** on a snippet shows everything needed to run it in plain R: the code of the enclosing scopes (with hidden parts) and its own, with the current values.
